title: Lender-Placed Flood Master Programs — Cancellation of Certificates on Loan Events
content:
A certificate under the **Lender-Placed Flood Master Programs** is also cancelled when the lender reports one of three loan events:

| Loan event reported by the lender | Cancellation effective on |
|---|---|
| The loan was paid off | The payoff date |
| Servicing of the loan moved to another servicer | The transfer date |
| A FEMA Letter of Map Amendment or Revision removed the building from the Special Flood Hazard Area | The letter's effective date |

**Credit.** Each uses its tier's refund method, pro rata on every tier: the credit is the annual premium multiplied by the days from the cancellation effective date to the certificate expiration date divided by the days in the certificate term, rounded to the cent. **This sentence is no longer in force for a loan event that the lender reports on the day it takes effect, on the certificate most recently issued under the program; any other loan-event cancellation keeps this pro rata credit.**

**Paid claims.** A certificate with a paid claim earns its full premium on every tier: when a claim on the certificate has a net payment above zero — the claim payments issued on the certificate less the payments voided, over the whole life of that certificate — no credit is given for these three reasons.

## Points of judgement

- *A claim payment on the certificate was issued and later voided in full.* The net payment is zero, not above zero, so the bar on credit does not apply.
- *A claim payment was issued and only part of it was voided.* The net payment is above zero, and no credit is given for a loan payoff, a servicing transfer or a removal from the area.

superseded_clauses: Each uses its tier's refund method, PRO_RATA: the credit is the annual premium multiplied by the days from the cancellation effective date to the certificate expiration date divided by the days in the certificate term, rounded to the cent.
